Introduction

This report documents the fecundity process as it is currently implemented for Eriogonum longifolium. It is intended as an exploratory description of the current data structure and fitted fecundity components.

The report focuses on:

  1. flowering probability,
  2. number of scapes conditional on flowering,
  3. the scapes-to-recruits transition,
  4. recruit size distribution, and
  5. how these components are combined in the IPM fecundity process.

Only the currently selected models are fitted here. No model selection is repeated in this report.

Setup

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.align = 'center')

library(MASS)
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)

set.seed(100)
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

v_head <- 'archbold'
v_species <- 'Eriogonum longifolium'
v_years_re <- c()

v_sp_abb <- tolower(
  gsub(
    ' ',
    '',
    paste(
      substr(
        unlist(strsplit(v_species, ' ')),
        1, 2),
      collapse = '')))

v_ggp_suffix <- paste(
  tools::toTitleCase(v_head),
  '-',
  v_species)

dir_data <- file.path(
  'C:', 'code', 'RUPDemo_IPMs',
  v_head,
  'data',
  v_sp_abb)

data_file <- file.path(
  dir_data,
  paste0(
    'ab_',
    v_sp_abb,
    '_df_workdata_260820.csv'))

if (!file.exists(data_file)) {
  stop(
    'Data file not found: ',
    data_file,
    '\nKnit this report from the project root or update data_file.')
}

ctrl_glmer <- glmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa',
  optCtrl = list(
    maxfun = 2e5))

ctrl_re <- glmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa',
  optCtrl = list(
    maxfun = 2e5))

Data

The same working-data file and basic data preparation used in the current IPM analysis are used here.

disturbance_case_levels <- c(
  'Undisturbed',
  'Current-year fire',
  'Previous-year fire',
  'Fire in both years')

df <- read.csv(
  data_file) %>%
  mutate(
    disturbance = as.numeric(
      dist_transition),
    disturbance_prev = as.numeric(
      disturbance_prev),
    year = as.integer(year),
    row_type = as.character(
      row_type),
    disturbance_case = factor(
      paste0(
        disturbance,
        disturbance_prev),
      levels = c(
        '00', '10', '01', '11'),
      labels = disturbance_case_levels)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !(year %in% v_years_re))

df_ind <- df %>%
  filter(
    row_type == 'individual')

df_re_all <- df %>%
  filter(
    row_type == 'recruitment')

df_re <- df_re_all %>%
  filter(
    recruitment_complete,
    !is.na(recruits_simple))

Fecundity as currently implemented

The current fecundity process has three fitted demographic components followed by a recruit-size distribution:

  • flowering probability is modeled at the individual-year level;
  • scape number is modeled at the individual-year level conditional on flowering;
  • scapes and recruits are summed to the site-population-year level for the scapes-to-recruits model;
  • the fitted recruitment relationship is converted back to recruits per scape before entering the individual-level IPM fecundity calculation;
  • recruits are distributed across recruit size using the observed seedling-size distribution.

Previous-year fire is used in flowering and scape production. Current-year fire is used in the scapes-to-recruits component.

Flowering probability

Flowering data

df_fl <- df %>%
  filter(
    state == 'active',
    !is.na(flower),
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0),
    is.finite(logsize_t0_2),
    is.finite(logsize_t0_3),
    !is.na(disturbance_prev)) %>%
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    disturbance_prev = as.numeric(
      disturbance_prev))

Selected flowering model

The currently selected flowering model contains cubic size dependence, previous-year fire, and a year random intercept.

mod_fl_bestfit <- glmer(
  flower ~
    logsize_t0 +
    logsize_t0_2 +
    logsize_t0_3 +
    disturbance_prev +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_fl,
  family = binomial,
  control = ctrl_glmer)

formula(mod_fl_bestfit)
## flower ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3 + disturbance_prev + 
##     (1 | year)
summary(mod_fl_bestfit)

##     (1 | year)

Flowering data coverage

The first table shows individual-year records. The second removes repeated individuals within a quadrat-year and therefore shows the disturbance coverage at the quadrat-year level.

df_fl %>%
  count(
    disturbance_prev,
    name = 'n_individual_years') %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  print(n = Inf)
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   disturbance_prev n_individual_years
##              <dbl>              <int>
## 1                0              12717
## 2                1               1297
df_fl %>%
  distinct(
    site,
    pop,
    qu,
    year,
    disturbance_prev) %>%
  count(
    disturbance_prev,
    name = 'n_quadrat_years') %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  print(n = Inf)
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   disturbance_prev n_quadrat_years
##              <dbl>           <int>
## 1                0             997
## 2                1              84

Mean flowering relationship

The mean relationship uses fixed effects only. The year random effect is excluded with re.form = NA.

df_fl_mean_pred <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  logsize_t0 = seq(
    min(
      df_fl$logsize_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    max(
      df_fl$logsize_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = 100),
  disturbance_prev = c(0, 1)) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
    logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3,
    year = factor(
      levels(df_fl$year)[1],
      levels = levels(df_fl$year)))

df_fl_mean_pred <- df_fl_mean_pred %>%
  mutate(
    flower = predict(
      mod_fl_bestfit,
      newdata = df_fl_mean_pred,
      type = 'response',
      re.form = NA,
      allow.new.levels = TRUE))

df_fl_mean_binned <- df_fl %>%
  mutate(
    bin = cut(
      logsize_t0,
      breaks = 10)) %>%
  group_by(
    bin,
    disturbance_prev) %>%
  summarise(
    logsize_t0 = mean(
      logsize_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    flower = mean(
      flower,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(logsize_t0),
    n > 0)

fig_fl_mean <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = df_fl_mean_binned,
    aes(
      logsize_t0,
      flower,
      color = factor(
        disturbance_prev))) +
  geom_line(
    data = df_fl_mean_pred,
    aes(
      logsize_t0,
      flower,
      color = factor(
        disturbance_prev),
      linetype = factor(
        disturbance_prev)),
    linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      '0' = 'black',
      '1' = 'red'),
    labels = c(
      '0' = 'No previous fire',
      '1' = 'Previous-year fire'),
    name = 'Fire') +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      '0' = 'solid',
      '1' = 'dashed'),
    labels = c(
      '0' = 'No previous fire',
      '1' = 'Previous-year fire'),
    name = 'Fire') +
  labs(
    title = 'Mean flowering probability',
    subtitle = 'Fixed effects only - no year effect',
    x = expression(
      'log(diameter)'[t0]),
    y = 'Flowering probability') +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_bw()

fig_fl_mean

Flowering relationships by year

The same model is shown for all years in one panel. The corresponding year random effect is included with re.form = NULL.

df_fl_year_pred <- map_dfr(
  levels(df_fl$year),
  function(year_i) {
    df_i <- df_fl %>%
      filter(year == year_i)

    x <- seq(
      min(df_i$logsize_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(df_i$logsize_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      length.out = 100)

    pred_i <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  logsize_t0 = x,
  disturbance_prev = c(0, 1)) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
    logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3,
    year = factor(
      year_i,
      levels = levels(df_fl$year)))

pred_i %>%
  mutate(
    flower = predict(
      mod_fl_bestfit,
      newdata = pred_i,
      type = 'response',
      re.form = NULL,
      allow.new.levels = TRUE))
  })

df_fl_year_obs <- df_fl %>%

    flower = mean(flower, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(logsize_t0),

fig_fl_year <- ggplot() +

Number of scapes conditional on flowering

Scape-number data

df_fl_cond <- df_fl %>%
  filter(
    flower == 1,
    !is.na(fl_nr),
    fl_nr > 0,
    fl_nr == round(fl_nr),
    !is.na(disturbance_prev)) %>%
  mutate(
    year = factor(year))

Selected scape-number model

The currently selected model contains cubic size dependence, previous-year fire, and a year random intercept.

mod_fl_n_bestfit <- glmer.nb(
  fl_nr ~
    logsize_t0 +
    logsize_t0_2 +
    logsize_t0_3 +
    disturbance_prev +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_fl_cond,
  control = ctrl_glmer)

formula(mod_fl_n_bestfit)

Scape bookkeeping

The recruitment rows contain nr_scapes, while individual plant records contain fl_nr. The following check compares both quantities after individual scape counts are summed to the quadrat-year level.

df_scapes_ind_quad <- df_ind %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(fl_nr)) %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    pop,
    qu,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_individual_records = n(),
    scapes_from_individuals = sum(
      fl_nr,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop')

df_scapes_re_quad <- df_re %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(nr_scapes)) %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    pop,
    qu,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    scapes_from_recruitment = sum(
      nr_scapes,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    recruits = sum(
      recruits_simple,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop')

df_scape_compare <- full_join(
  df_scapes_ind_quad,
  df_scapes_re_quad,
  by = c(
    'site',
    'pop',
    'qu',
    'year')) %>%
  mutate(
    difference =
      scapes_from_recruitment -
      scapes_from_individuals)

df_scape_compare %>%
  summarise(
    n_quadrat_years = n(),
    n_both_available = sum(
      !is.na(
        scapes_from_individuals) &
        !is.na(
          scapes_from_recruitment)),
    mean_individual_scapes = mean(
      scapes_from_individuals,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_recruitment_scapes = mean(
      scapes_from_recruitment,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_difference = mean(
      difference,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    max_abs_difference = max(
      abs(difference),
      na.rm = TRUE),
    correlation = cor(
      scapes_from_individuals,
      scapes_from_recruitment,
      use = 'complete.obs')) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  print(n = Inf)

Scapes to recruits

Recruitment data and aggregation

The current scapes-to-recruits model is fitted after aggregation to site-population-year. Scapes and recruits are summed over recruitment quadrats.

A site-population-year is classified as disturbed when at least one contributing quadrat has disturbance == 1. This is the current aggregation used in the IPM.

df_sc2re <- df_re %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(nr_scapes),
    !is.na(recruits_simple)) %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    pop,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    total_scapes = sum(
      nr_scapes),
    recruit_count = sum(
      recruits_simple),
    disturbance = case_when(
      any(
        disturbance == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1,
      any(
        is.na(disturbance)) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 0),
    disturbance_prev = case_when(
      any(
        disturbance_prev == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1,
      any(
        is.na(disturbance_prev)) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 0),
    .groups = 'drop')

df_sc2re_mod <- df_sc2re %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(total_scapes),
    !is.na(recruit_count),
    !is.na(disturbance),
    !(year %in% v_years_re)) %>%
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    disturbance = as.numeric(
      disturbance),
    disturbance_prev = as.numeric(
      disturbance_prev))

Selected scapes-to-recruits model

The currently selected recruitment model uses log-transformed scape number, current-year disturbance, their interaction, and a year random intercept.

mod_re_bestfit <- glmer.nb(
  recruit_count ~
    log1p(total_scapes) *
    disturbance +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_sc2re_mod,
  control = ctrl_re)

formula(mod_re_bestfit)
## recruit_count ~ log1p(total_scapes) * disturbance + (1 | year)
summary(mod_re_bestfit)
## Generalized linear mixed model fit by maximum likelihood (Laplace
##   Approximation) [glmerMod]

## Formula: recruit_count ~ log1p(total_scapes) * disturbance + (1 | year)
##    Data: df_sc2re_mod
## Control: ctrl_re

##

re_year_sd <- if (
    'year' %in%
      names(
        VarCorr(

    VarCorr(

    'stddev')[1]
} else {

}

Recruitment aggregation checks

Mixed-fire site-population-years

The following table identifies site-population-years in which both disturbed and undisturbed quadrats contribute before aggregation.

df_f2r_fire_trace <- df_re %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(nr_scapes),
    !is.na(recruits_simple)) %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    pop,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_quadrats = n_distinct(qu),
    n_fire_0 = sum(
      disturbance == 0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_fire_1 = sum(
      disturbance == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_fire_na = sum(
      is.na(disturbance)),
    mixed_fire =
      n_fire_0 > 0 &
      n_fire_1 > 0,
    proportion_fire = if_else(
      n_fire_0 + n_fire_1 > 0,
      n_fire_1 /
        (n_fire_0 + n_fire_1),
      NA_real_),
    disturbance_used = case_when(
      any(
        disturbance == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE) ~ 1,
      any(
        is.na(disturbance)) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ 0),
    total_scapes = sum(
      nr_scapes,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    recruit_count = sum(
      recruits_simple,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop')

df_f2r_fire_trace %>%
  summarise(
    n_site_pop_years = n(),
    n_mixed_fire = sum(
      mixed_fire,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    p_mixed_fire = mean(
      mixed_fire,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_prop_fire_when_disturbed = mean(
      proportion_fire[
        disturbance_used == 1],
      na.rm = TRUE),
    min_prop_fire_when_disturbed = min(
      proportion_fire[
        disturbance_used == 1],
      na.rm = TRUE),
    max_prop_fire_when_disturbed = max(
      proportion_fire[
        disturbance_used == 1],
      na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  print(n = Inf)

Conversion back to individual fecundity

The recruitment model is fitted at site-population-year level. The IPM, however, requires expected recruitment from an individual plant.

The current implementation therefore predicts recruitment across the common observed distribution of site-population-year scape totals and divides the sum of predicted recruits by the total number of observed scapes. This produces one mean recruits-per-scape conversion for each current-fire state.

get_recr_per_scape <- function(
    disturbance_i,
    year_i = NULL) {

  df_i <- df_sc2re_mod %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance =
        disturbance_i)

  if (is.null(year_i)) {
    re_form_i <- NA
  } else if (
      as.character(year_i) %in%
        levels(df_sc2re_mod$year)) {

    df_i <- df_i %>%
      mutate(
        year = factor(
          as.character(year_i),
          levels = levels(
            df_sc2re_mod$year)))

    re_form_i <- NULL
  } else {
    re_form_i <- NA
  }

  pred_i <- predict(
    mod_re_bestfit,
    newdata = df_i,
    type = 'response',
    re.form = re_form_i,
    allow.new.levels = TRUE)

  total_scapes_i <- sum(
    df_i$total_scapes,
    na.rm = TRUE)

  if (
      !is.finite(
        total_scapes_i) ||
      total_scapes_i <= 0) {
    return(0)
  }

  sum(
    pred_i,
    na.rm = TRUE) /
    total_scapes_i
}

recr_per_scape_0 <-
  get_recr_per_scape(0)

recr_per_scape_1 <-
  get_recr_per_scape(1)

tibble(
  disturbance = c(
    'No current fire',
    'Current-year fire'),
  recruits_per_scape = c(
    recr_per_scape_0,
    recr_per_scape_1)) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
## # A tibble: 2 × 2
##   disturbance       recruits_per_scape
##   <chr>                          <dbl>
## 1 No current fire                0.281
## 2 Current-year fire              1.19

For an individual of size \(x\), this conversion is combined with flowering probability and expected scape number:

\[ E(R \mid x) = P(\mathrm{flower}\mid x) \times E(\mathrm{scapes}\mid \mathrm{flower},x) \times E(\mathrm{recruits\ per\ scape}). \]

Thus, the site-population-year recruitment model is brought back to the individual fecundity calculation through the recruits-per-scape term.

Recruit size distribution

Recruit size is taken from individual records classified as seedlings.

df_re_size <- df_ind %>%
  filter(
    recruit_type == 'seedling',
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0))

recr_sz <- mean(
  df_re_size$logsize_t0,
  na.rm = TRUE)

recr_sd <- sd(
  df_re_size$logsize_t0,
  na.rm = TRUE)

recr_min <- min(
  df_re_size$logsize_t0,
  na.rm = TRUE)

recr_max <- max(
  df_re_size$logsize_t0,
  na.rm = TRUE)

normal_mass_observed_range <-
  pnorm(
    recr_max,
    mean = recr_sz,
    sd = recr_sd) -
  pnorm(
    recr_min,
    mean = recr_sz,
    sd = recr_sd)

tibble(
  n_seedlings = nrow(
    df_re_size),
  mean_logsize = recr_sz,
  sd_logsize = recr_sd,
  minimum_logsize = recr_min,
  maximum_logsize = recr_max,
  fitted_normal_mass_inside_observed_range =
    normal_mass_observed_range) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
## # A tibble: 1 × 6
##   n_seedlings mean_logsize sd_logsize minimum_logsize maximum_logsize
##         <int>        <dbl>      <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl>
## 1         108        0.359      0.474           -1.20            1.79
## # ℹ 1 more variable: fitted_normal_mass_inside_observed_range <dbl>

Observed recruit-size distribution

The histogram shows the observed seedling-size distribution. The line is the normal distribution defined by the observed mean and standard deviation, which is the distributional form used for recruits in the IPM.

df_re_size_density <- tibble(
  logsize_t0 = seq(
    recr_min,
    recr_max,
    length.out = 300)) %>%
  mutate(
    density = dnorm(
      logsize_t0,
      mean = recr_sz,
      sd = recr_sd))

Fecundity bookkeeping summary

The current fecundity process can therefore be summarized as follows.

fecundity_bookkeeping <- tibble(
  component = c(
    'Flowering probability',
    'Scapes conditional on flowering',
    'Scapes to recruits',
    'Recruit size'),
  fitted_or_estimated_level = c(
    'Individual-year',
    'Individual-year',
    'Site-population-year',
    'Individual seedlings'),
  disturbance = c(
    'Previous-year fire',
    'Previous-year fire',
    'Current-year fire',
    'None'),
  IPM_quantity = c(
    'Probability of flowering',
    'Expected scapes conditional on flowering',
    'Recruits per scape',
    'Recruit size density'))

fecundity_bookkeeping %>%
  print(n = Inf)
## # A tibble: 4 × 4
##   component                      fitted_or_estimated_…¹ disturbance IPM_quantity
##   <chr>                          <chr>                  <chr>       <chr>       
## 1 Flowering probability          Individual-year        Previous-y… Probability…
## 2 Scapes conditional on floweri… Individual-year        Previous-y… Expected sc…
## 3 Scapes to recruits             Site-population-year   Current-ye… Recruits pe…
## 4 Recruit size                   Individual seedlings   None        Recruit siz…
## # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​fitted_or_estimated_level

The fecundity contribution of an individual of size \(x\) to recruits of size \(y\) is represented by:

\[ F(y,x) = P(\mathrm{flower}\mid x) \times E(\mathrm{scapes}\mid \mathrm{flower},x) \times E(\mathrm{recruits\ per\ scape}) \times f_{\mathrm{recruit\ size}}(y). \]

This section describes the current implementation only. The preceding tables and figures document the observational levels, disturbance coverage, fitted mean relationships, yearly relationships, recruitment aggregation, and recruit size distribution used in that implementation.
